Thorens TD 160 With ADC arm Grado FTE+1 cartridge.

Marantz PM30 amp Marantz CD40 & Tannoy spkrs These items are probably more like 20/25 yrs old

Shortly after puchase of the Thorens I was introduced to the buzz and click free world of cd'd I started purchasing cd's replacing and expanding my music collection. Then due to a series of house moves the vinyl ended up in storage for close to 30 yrs.

I will preface the next bit with this I am not nor claim to be any kind of audiophile, all the above was the best I could afford at the time and well short of the best available in the day.

Fast forward to a year or so ago I saw on ebay that early pressings of the Wall were fetching silly prices.I started going down the rabbit hole of matrix no's first pressings which engineers and which pressing plant etc.

Cutting to the chase. I checked through my LP's, I found two versions of the Wall one it turns out was a first press. I listened on the above system I also compared it to the cd.

I was blown away that even on what was a 'budget system' that a)The first press was so noticeably better than the later press and b) just how sterile the cd sounded in comparison.

I had put to the back of my mind the old vinyl versus cd debate but it explained what I considered the slightly puzzling continued existence / resurgence of vinyl

TLDR Audiophiles are right about vinyl.Those eager to write it's obituary in the 80's were wrong.

I don't know if this is the content you want on this sub but it's the nearest one to my rant I could find.

You had some very nice equipment. I can't afford thorens turntables or tannoy speakers. Those are really nice! I've searched high and low for years and only once did I see a thorens appear on Craigslist for 30bucks! Sadly I didn't get to it first. I'm still searching for 60s MCINTOSH gear. Vinyl has the best sound of any media out there, nothing beats an analog signal.

It was my only luxury at the time. For it's time it was only considered mid priced. My only regret at the time is that I couldn't afford a Quad amp & pre-amp.

I was a skeptic about the merits of vinyl. I couldn't wait to get get rid of the hiss pop & click of all my earlier LPs One of the reasons I purchased a good arm cartidge etc.was to preserve any later purchases.

Agreed on the analog thing. It explains the resilience in the vinyl recordings.
Yah having a good tone arm, cartridge and needle make a big difference in vinyl quality. It takes a lot of tinkering to get it right but to me that ads to the experience and value.

I still have the one I made and finally settled on It's a long time ago but I think it was an averaged version.
